# `fluxsim apply`

Write every run artifact of a recorded plan: the population, the events, the emit streams and their seam attestations, the run digest and the receipt. With --run-id, commits what plan staged after checking the plan, the bundle and every staged file, and generates nothing; with no staged rows it executes the plan again. Refuses when the plan or the bundle has moved since the plan was recorded. A run whose bundle declares generator plugins, once committed, is kept as it stands: apply never asks the plugin for its rows again or writes the run directory over, and with --sink it delivers the run's files. A child table that a counts entry lays out comes out grouped by parent in row order, as a table loaded parent by parent does; a consumer that needs another order sorts it. The child's own key is laid out from the row index, so a number or date key in ascending order gives a parent's children consecutive keys, and a text or UUID key, permuted, does not.

## Synopsis

```text
fluxsim apply [options] <bundle>
```

## Examples

```bash
# apply the plan recorded under that id (`plan` prints it)
fluxsim apply ./bundle --run-id de72fa4b22711c52

# write the first of four shares of that run (no receipt; a share is not a run)
fluxsim apply ./bundle --run-id de72fa4b22711c52 --shard 1/4

# apply the run whole and write every stream as Parquet
fluxsim apply ./bundle --run-id de72fa4b22711c52 --sink parquet:./out/parquet
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `bundle` | path to the FLUX bundle directory |

## Options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--run-id` | `RUN_ID` | the run id to act on (as reported by `fluxsim plan`/`fluxsim run`) (default: take a fresh plan first) |
| `--simulation-id` | `SIMULATION_ID` | which Simulation document to resolve (default: the bundle's only one) |
| `--zone` | `ZONE` | declared run zone, for sovereignty checks |
| `--shard` | `I/N` | make only the I-th of N contiguous shares of every emit's rows and write them as emits/&lt;exposeId&gt;.shard-I-of-N.ndjson; the shares joined in order are the bytes of the run's emit streams. A share is part of a run: no run digest and no receipt |
| `--sink` | `NAME:TARGET` | also write every stream to a sink, after the run is written: parquet:DIR or arrow-ipc:DIR (a directory, or an s3://, gs://, az:// or abfs:// prefix), adbc:DRIVER, iceberg:CATALOG/NAMESPACE or delta:DIR (a directory or an object store URL) (`fluxsim plugins` lists them) |
| `--sink-opt` | `KEY=VALUE` | a --sink setting, repeatable, for example row-group-size=100000 or uri=sim.duckdb; never a password: pass uri-env=VAR instead |
| `--allow-generator` | `NAME` | allow the generator plugin of that entry-point name to be imported and run, when apply generates the rows rather than committing a stage; repeat it for each plugin the bundle declares under generators (without it the command is refused, FLX-3119, before anything is imported); a plugin is trusted code that runs with your rights, so name only plugins you have reviewed; no environment variable and no bundle key allows one |
| `--scale` | `F` | multiply every emit's rows, the records bounds of its fidelity block and the span of every integer or decimal key column that declares a range, by F (above 0, at most 1000000); the plan records it and apply reads it back, and 1 changes nothing; a table built from the run's events is left as it is; read only when a fresh plan is taken, since the plan of --run-id records its own |
| `--timings` |  | print where the time went (load, compile, each emit, framing, attestation); the numbers are wall-clock seconds, reported and recorded nowhere in a run's files |
| `--jobs` | `N` | the most processes that may generate the rows of an emit declared by statistics: a number (never more than one per CPU) or auto for one per CPU; the run summary says how many it used, and the rows and every digest are the same whatever the number (default: FLUX_JOBS, else 1) |
| `--strict-coverage` |  | refuse the run when a column falls back to a type default (an optional column nothing maps onto, a DATE or TIMESTAMP column with no declaration of its own), with a table of every such column (FLX-3304), or when the contract declares what the run does not generate, such as a check without generates or, on kernel 0.1.0 or in a Simulation that does not declare copies: true, sharedColumns or sharedAttribute (FLX-3305), before any row is drawn; a Simulation can ask for the same with strictCoverage: true in its extensions; without either the plan names those columns and goes on, and with this flag the rows and every digest are the same either way |
| `--profile` | `PATH` | the profile document the Simulation pins under extensions['com.agentics.flux/1'].profile (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md); refused when its digest is not the pinned one, and when the Simulation pins none; read only for a fresh plan, so refused with --run-id |
| `--state-dir` | `STATE_DIR` | run-state directory (default: ./.flux) |
| `-j, --json` |  | emit machine-readable JSON |
